messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike from one free-tier key that knocked over the shared GPU pool for ~20s earlier. Not a scheduled test, looked like a customer script gone wild.

mira: Oof. Which pool/region?

alex: us-west-2, pool-regular-1. Metrics show one key used 120k tokens in 2m while the org median was 1.2k.

jon: Was that per-org or a single API key? Free keys should have stricter per-key shaping.

alex: single key. Per-org quota wasn't exceeded. We rely on per-org first, per-key second right now, which let that blast through.

mira: Is this because burst allowance is tied to plan band rather than key identity? Free plan gets small burst but it's shared across keys in the org.

samir: We should add a short-term spike protection that: 1) detects >X tokens in Ys per key, 2) applies a fast soft-throttle that decays over time, 3) keeps org-level metrics intact for billing.

lina: Agree. Also want telemetry so console shows "spike-suppressed" events per key and org for debugging. UX: show a little red dot and hover text with counts.

jon: Idea for heuristic: maintain an exponential moving window for each key; if instantaneous rate > baseline * multiplier then apply spike-smoothing token-bucket with small refill. Baseline computed from 1h median.

mira: Sounds good. Need to be careful with enterprise customers — we may need opt-out or whitelisting for dedicated capacity. For hosted free/pro we can be stricter.

samir: Draft policy sample config (P0):

```json
{
  "name": "per_key_spike_guard",
  "scope": "per_key",
  "detection_window_seconds": 30,
  "baseline_window_seconds": 3600,
  "burst_multiplier": 4,
  "soft_throttle_type": "token_bucket",
  "soft_throttle_capacity": 8000,
  "decay_seconds": 300,
  "plan_overrides": {
    "free": { "burst_multiplier": 2, "soft_throttle_capacity": 4000 },
    "pro": { "burst_multiplier": 3, "soft_throttle_capacity": 8000 },
    "enterprise": { "exempt": true }
  }
}
```

alex: Love the plan_overrides field. Let's default enterprise to exempt and have a telemetry flag for when infra applied a fallback to org-level limits instead.

lina: For console: add a per-route timeline that shows sudden per-key suppressions. We already have per-route token breakdown — add event markers that link to key ID and sample requests masked.

jon: Rollout approach: canary in us-west-2 small fraction (5% keys) for 24h, then 25% -> 100% if no false positives. ops-bot can handle gradual gating.

samir: Also add an API for customers to request temporary burst raises (ttl-limited) via console for pro/enterprise. Free stays auto-only. That helps UX.

mira: We need to avoid double-throttling: per-key soft throttle should be layered before per-org hard quota enforcement and before gateway rate limits. Order of enforcement matters.

alex: Agreed. Enforcement order proposal: 1) auth/gateway rate limits (global) 2) per-key spike-guard (soft) 3) per-key hard quota 4) per-org quota 5) plan-level SLA guard -> fallback to cheaper region/model.

jon: Add a short reason code to responses so callers can log: e.g., 429 with header `x-rbq-throttle-reason: per_key_spike_suppressed_v1`. Saves support time.

lina: And in the billing/telemetry pipeline tag suppressed tokens separately so we don't bill suppressed tokens for free tier, but we do for pro/enterprise depending on policy. Need product decision.

samir: Product: free keys — suppressed tokens not billable; pro — billable but flagged; enterprise — billable with optional crediting on request. This maps to pricing plans.

mira: Can we run a dry-run mode where we emit telemetry but don't actually throttle? Useful for tuning thresholds.

ops-bot: deploy: spike-guard v0.1 config pushed to staging in us-west-2 dry-run mode by @ops-bot. CI tests passed.

alex: Nice. Who will monitor the canary?

jon: I'll watch s-metrics and set alert if key-level P95 throttle events > 0.1% of requests for the canary set. Also dashboard panels for suppressed tokens and false-positive overrides.

lina: I'll mock up console markers and add a tooltip copy.

samir: Follow-ups: (1) add reason header and docs, (2) implement plan overrides mapping to billing flags, (3) telemetry schema change to include suppressed/bypassed flags, (4) rollout plan in infra runbook.

mira: Can someone file the lightweight RFC so we can attach the config and rollout checklist? Alex or Samir?

alex: I'll open RFC with the config above + tests and canary playbook.

samir: Great. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: NOTE: canary dry-run will emit events to /internal/telemetry/spike-guard/dry-run. Use `rbqctl events watch spike-guard` to stream samples.
